title: Which propagation, when
idea: Each kind of over-the-horizon propagation has a giveaway: how often it happens, how it sounds, or what causes it.

rows: Occasional strong signals beyond the horizon on 10, 6 and 2 m
Regular VHF/UHF contacts out to about 300 miles
Signals getting past a ridge or other obstruction
Long-distance 10 or 6 m at the sunspot peak
The F region, from dawn to just after sunset

config.heading: What's carrying the signal?
config.lead: Pick what you're hearing. For F-region openings, set the band, sunspots and time.

situations.label: Sudden strong signals beyond the horizon
situations.title: Sporadic E
situations.text: Occasional strong signals from beyond the radio horizon on the 10, 6 and 2 meter bands.

situations.label: Regular VHF/UHF out to about 300 miles
situations.title: Tropospheric ducting
situations.text: Over-the-horizon VHF and UHF to about 300 miles on a regular basis. It's caused by temperature inversions in the atmosphere.

situations.label: Raspy, distorted VHF signals
situations.title: Auroral backscatter
situations.text: VHF signals off the aurora are distorted, with a raspy sound.

situations.label: Getting past a ridge between stations
situations.title: Knife-edge diffraction
situations.text: A sharp edge, like a ridge, can bend signals over the obstruction.

situations.label: Short bursts off meteor trails
situations.title: Meteor scatter
situations.text: The band best suited for it is 6 meters.

situations.label: Long distance through the F region
situations.title: F region

rules.title: Open: long distance via the F region
rules.text: High sunspots and daytime: the best time for long-distance 10 meter contacts, and at the sunspot peak 6 meters can open too.

rules.title: Less likely at night
rules.text: The best time for 10 meter F-region contacts is from dawn to shortly after sunset.

rules.title: Unlikely with low sunspots
rules.text: Long-distance F-region openings on these bands come with high sunspot activity.

rules.title: Not via the F region
rules.text: At the peak of the sunspot cycle, the bands that open through the F region are 6 and 10 meters.

compare.how: 10 and 6 m at the sunspot peak, in daytime.

traps.why: Occasional strong signals beyond the horizon on 10, 6 and 2 m is the signature of sporadic E.
Regular VHF/UHF to about 300 miles is tropospheric ducting, down low in the atmosphere.
Sunspots drive the F region. Ducting comes from temperature inversions.
Meteor scatter works best on 6 meters.

traps.wrong: From shortly after sunset to dawn during periods of high sunspot activity
traps.why: Right sunspots, wrong time. 10 m F-region contacts are best from dawn to just after sunset.

traps.wrong: They are often received from 10,000 miles or more
traps.why: The giveaway for auroral signals is the sound: distorted and raspy.
